newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign funds lift Indian shares, range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds lift Indian shares, range-bound.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) Indian shares end higher in tight range
** Foreign funds save day in sluggish market
** Undercurrent suspect, seen adrift
** Reuter poll shows company profit growth slowing
** Bombay share index rises 6.64 pts, Delhi index 2.62 pts,
Calcutta index 1.44 pts and Madras index 1.89 pts
** National exchange index gains 0.07 pts
Selective buying by foreign institutional investors pulled Indian shares to positive territory at close on Tuesday but the undercurrent was suspect, brokers said.
A slowing economy, shrinking company profit growth this year and uncertain political prospects discouraged fresh purchases, they said.
But fresh selling was limited in the depressed market with buyers emerging at lower levels, the brokers said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index rose 6.64 points, or 0.20 percent, to 3,337.73.
Turnover was 3.38 billion rupees in 23.7 million shares.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index ended 0.07 points higher at 968.91.
The net traded value was 9.13 billion rupees in 47.8 million shares.

A Reuter poll of 14 leading securities houses projected an average 20.6 percent rise in the net profit of 30 index firms during the first half ending September 30, 1996 from around 40 percent a year ago.
Net sales growth was pegged at a modest 16.5 percent.
Analysts said declining global prices of commodities like petrochemicals, aluminium and steel coupled with cuts in import duties of these products would hit several index firms.
But banks and auto firms are expected to fare better.

SBI, India's largest bank, is projected to see net profit soaring 178 percent in the first half -- thanks to sharply reduced depreciation provision on government securities, analysts said. SBI was up 1.25 rupees at 262.50.
Bajaj Auto rose 15.50 rupees to 990.75, ITC 4.25 to 298.25, M&M 2.25 to 330.50, Reliance 2.0 to 197, TISCO 1.75 to 173.50, Ranbaxy 2.75 to 609.75 and ACC 18.0 to 1,869.25.
--RANJIT GANGADHARAN, Bombay Newsroom +91-22-265-9000
